1.why: Every MFA endpoint passes through owner(), which requires the server-owned session to be at stage "mfa" with userId === ACCOUNT.id, and no user identifier is ever accepted from the client.

2.why: In production the identity code is a random 6-digit value hashed per session and TOTP is derived from the session's own encrypted secret, but TEST mode is the default whenever NODE_ENV !== "production", making "123456"/"654321" and fixed recovery codes valid for any session.

3.why: Enabling MFA (authenticator/verify) only mutates the current session object; there is no global/account-wide session invalidation, so any other existing sessions in the in-memory map remain usable.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored only as AES-GCM ciphertext (encrypt/decrypt with a non-extractable key) and backup codes are stored as peppered SHA-256 hashes, with only hashes compared on verification.

5.why: random() uses crypto.getRandomValues with modulo-bias rejection and the pepper/session/CSRF tokens are CSPRNG-derived, but in the default TEST mode secrets, identity codes and recovery codes are hard-coded constants.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage or document.cookie use exists and the session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict; only in-memory JS variables (csrf, window._savedCodes) and test-mode console/DOM log entries hold sensitive values.

7.why: emailInput, passwordInput, otpInput and recoveryInput apply length bounds and strict regexes server-side, rejecting rather than truncating, and there is no SQL layer at all (in-memory Map).

8.why: All dynamic values are escaped through e() before insertHTML/innerHTML, log() uses textContent, and a nonce-based CSP with script-src 'nonce-…' and base-uri 'none' blocks injected script.

9.why: The application performs no server-side redirects and no user-controlled navigation (only location.reload()), so no open-redirect path exists, though no explicit allow-list mechanism is coded either.

10.why: headers() sets CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy on every response.

11.why: secureCookie() emits `mfa_session=…; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=…` and logout clears it with the same attributes.

12.why: Server errors return generic messages with no stack traces and nothing sensitive appears in URLs, but the default TEST mode returns testIdentityOtp/testAuthenticatorCode and prints OTPs, provisioning URIs and recovery codes to console.log and an on-page log list.

13.why: Identity codes have a 10-minute expiry and are cleared on success, recovery codes are removed from backups once accepted, and pending setup details expire; however a valid TOTP code can be replayed within its ±30s window.

14.why: failed()/locked() enforce a 5-attempt threshold with a 10-minute lockout and 429 responses for identity, authenticator and recovery verification, though counters are per-session so a fresh cookie resets them.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a new 48-char id via make() with a fresh cookie, idle (20 min) and absolute (8 h) timeouts are checked in get(), and logout deletes the session and expires the cookie; the second-factor step rotates only the CSRF token, not the session id.
